ops.note:
Verified against released ccx v0.39.0 in a fresh `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/yasyf/cc-context.git` with `.git/.graphite_repo_config` planted — a repo Graphite demonstrably refuses (`gt auth` exits 1, "does not have the necessary permissions to submit PRs to yasyf/cc-context"). A logging `gt` shim ahead on PATH recorded every gt invocation.

**Forms no commit on a gt branch: yes.** Both ships landed on plain `main` (`git branch --show-current` → `main`; commits 1ce81d7, b562226). Report line: `lane git (ERROR: Graphite does not have the necessary permissions…) · hooks ok · committed 1ce81d7 · branch main · not pushed`.

**Makes no gt call — measured under both readings, since the wording is ambiguous now that the gate itself probes.** First ship in a cold repo: exactly one gt call, `gt auth --no-interactive`, the read-only status probe the gate needs to reach its verdict (it rewrites `.graphite_pr_info` and notably not `.graphite_repo_config`, so it cannot self-enable the lane). Zero gt mutation calls — no `gt create`, `gt modify`, `gt track`, or `gt submit`. Second ship, within the 1h denied-verdict TTL: **zero gt calls of any kind**, same demotion, same plain `main`.

So the strict reading holds in steady state and the substantive one — ship never uses gt as its VCS lane — holds always. Recording the distinction rather than asserting the strict wording unqualified: a reading of "no gt call" that forbids the probe would make the gate unimplementable, since the verdict cannot be reached without asking.
